QuestionQ201

Verified/Ensuring solution and operations excellence

You configured an autoscaling instance group to handle web traffic for an upcoming launch. After setting the instance group as a backend service for an HTTP(S) load balancer, you observe that virtual machine (VM) instances are terminated and relaunched every minute. The instances have no public IP addresses.

You verified with the curl command that every instance returns the appropriate web response. You want to make sure that the backend is configured properly.

What should you do?

Explanation

Google Cloud load-balancer backends require an ingress firewall rule that allows health-check probes to reach the backend VMs on the health-check protocol and port. If the probes are blocked, the default implied ingress-deny rule causes the backends to be considered unhealthy, which can trigger replacement of instances in a managed instance group. Public IP addresses are not required for backend VMs.

Learn more
  • Cloud Load Balancing firewall rules
  • Cloud Load Balancing health checks

QuestionQ202

Verified/Managing and provisioning a cloud solution infrastructure

Your company is expanding its AI-powered operations across the country and has selected accelerator-based compute for its AI workloads. The batch image-processing workloads are not time-sensitive and can tolerate interruptions. You need to quickly deploy cost-effective accelerator nodes for these batch tasks, while ensuring rapid deployment and data persistence when needed. What should you do?

Explanation

Spot VMs provide substantially discounted accelerator compute for fault-tolerant batch workloads, but they can be preempted at any time. Checkpointing preserves job progress, and attached persistent disks keep recoverable data after the Spot VM is stopped or preempted. Local SSD storage is temporary and is unsuitable where persistence is required.

QuestionQ203

Verified/Ensuring solution and operations excellence

To accelerate data retrieval, more vehicles will be upgraded with cellular connections and will be able to send data to the ETL process. The existing FTP process is error-prone and restarts transfer from the beginning of a file whenever a connection fails, which occurs frequently. You want to improve solution reliability and minimize data-transfer time over the cellular connections.

What should you do?

Explanation

Cloud Storage resumable uploads over HTTP(S) can resume after a communication failure from the byte offset already persisted, avoiding retransmission of the entire file. Placing uploads into regional buckets in the US, EU, and Asia keeps data transfer close to the vehicles’ geographic regions, minimizing latency and transfer time.

QuestionQ204

Verified/Analyzing and optimizing technical and business processes

You are developing an App Engine application that uses Cloud Datastore as its persistence layer. You must retrieve several root entities whose identifiers you have. You want to minimize the overhead of Cloud Datastore operations. What should you do?

Explanation

Cloud Datastore can retrieve multiple entities directly from their keys in a single batch lookup. Batch reads have the same operational overhead as a single operation, making them more efficient than separate get operations; queries are unnecessary when the entity identifiers are already known.

QuestionQ214

Refer to the EHR Healthcare case study. You must define the technical architecture for hybrid connectivity between EHR's on-premises systems and Google Cloud. You want to follow Google's recommended practices for production-level applications. Given the EHR Healthcare business and technical requirements, what should you do?

Explanation

Google’s production-level, 99.99% availability topology requires four Cloud Interconnect connections across two metropolitan areas: two Dedicated Interconnect connections in each metro, with the connections in a given metro placed in separate edge availability domains. This design protects connectivity from individual connection failures and avoids coordinated maintenance risk within a metro.

QuestionQ217

Your company runs its application workloads on Compute Engine. The applications are deployed in production, acceptance, and development environments. The production environment is business-critical and operates 24/7, whereas the acceptance and development environments are critical only during office hours. Your CFO has asked you to optimize these environments for cost savings during idle periods. What should you do?

Explanation

Stopping Compute Engine instances outside required hours removes VM CPU usage charges while they are stopped, although attached resources can still incur charges. Scheduling the acceptance and development environments to stop after office hours and start before office hours provides the required availability while reducing idle-time costs; production remains continuously available.

You have created several preemptible Linux virtual machine instances with Google Compute Engine. You want to shut down your application properly before the virtual machines are preempted.

What should you do?

Explanation

Compute Engine runs a Linux shutdown script specified in instance metadata with the shutdown-script key when a preemptible VM receives a preemption notice, providing a best-effort period of up to 30 seconds for cleanup. Supplying the script as the value of that metadata key during VM creation configures this behavior.

QuestionQ221

Verified/Ensuring solution and operations excellence

Your company has announced that it will outsource operations functions. You want to enable developers to easily stage new versions of a cloud-based application in the production environment, while allowing the outsourced operations team to independently promote staged versions to production. App Engine is a fully managed application platform that supports deploying a new version with traffic promotion disabled, so it can be staged in the production environment. This version-and-traffic model requires substantially less infrastructure and cluster administration than Compute Engine or Google Kubernetes Engine.

QuestionQ224

Verified/Designing for security and compliance

You deploy a custom Java application to Google App Engine. The deployment fails and produces the following stack trace.

What should you do?

Explanation

A SHA1 digest error from Java’s JAR verifier means a class file does not match the integrity digest stored in its signed JAR’s manifest. Re-signing the JAR files regenerates signature metadata that matches the deployed contents; missing JARs and changing the class compilation to MD5 do not correct that manifest-digest mismatch.

QuestionQ225

Your web application runs several VM instances in a VPC. You need to limit communication between instances to only the authorized paths and ports, without depending on static IP addresses or subnets because the application can autoscale. How should you restrict communication?

VPC firewall rules can use network tags as source and target selectors, so authorized traffic can be limited by protocol and port between appropriately tagged VM instances. Instances created through autoscaling receive the relevant tags without requiring static IP-address or subnet-based rules.

QuestionQ230

Verified/Designing for security and compliance

Your company has engaged an external auditing firm for a compliance audit. Company governance requires that external auditors be managed through one Google Group, which receives temporary, read-only access to a Cloud Storage bucket named audit-evidence-bucket.

Access must be traceable to each individual auditor’s identity and remain active only for the audit engagement, which lasts the full month of October. You need a secure access-control approach that avoids administrative overhead and meets the company’s governance policy. What should you do?

Explanation

A conditional IAM role binding can grant roles/storage.objectViewer to the required Google Group while a date/time condition limits authorization to the October audit window, such as request.time >= timestamp('YYYY-10-01T00:00:00Z') && request.time < timestamp('YYYY-11-01T00:00:00Z'). Auditors access Cloud Storage using their individual identities as group members, preserving per-user audit attribution. Cloud Storage supports date/time IAM Conditions on bucket policy bindings; uniform bucket-level access must be enabled for conditions set directly on a bucket.

QuestionQ234

You are building a globally scaled frontend for a legacy streaming-backend data API. The API requires events in strict chronological order and without repeated data for correct processing.

Which products should you deploy to guarantee once-only FIFO (first-in, first-out) data delivery?

Explanation

Pub/Sub alone only guarantees ordering and exactly-once delivery within a single region via ordering keys, so it cannot alone satisfy strict chronological, duplicate-free processing for a globally scaled frontend whose publishers/subscribers span regions. Cloud Dataflow adds the windowing, buffering, and stateful deduplication needed to reorder and dedupe a global stream before it reaches the legacy API, which is why Pub/Sub feeding into Dataflow is required.

QuestionQ242

During load testing, you see an error in the frontend service logs, but cannot locate the corresponding logs in downstream services to investigate the root cause because the logs are not correlated. You need to implement a solution that lets you follow one user request across every microservice involved in the transaction. Explanation

Cloud Trace uses trace context propagation, including the W3C traceparent header, to associate spans generated by calls across microservices with one trace ID. Cloud Logging can use that trace association to view all logs for the trace, providing request-level troubleshooting without implementing a custom correlation ID in every service.

You need to design a disaster recovery strategy that fulfills these strict BCP requirements. What should you do?

Explanation

A pre-established cross-region Cloud SQL read replica provides continuously replicated data in the secondary region and can be promoted to a writable primary during a regional outage. Defining the Compute Engine application infrastructure with Terraform enables the secondary environment to be recreated consistently within the two-hour recovery window. The replica’s replication lag must be monitored and kept within 15 minutes to meet the RPO. Google Cloud documents cross-region replicas and promotion as the Cloud SQL regional-disaster-recovery mechanism; backup/restore takes longer, and replica promotion is required before the secondary database can accept writes.

QuestionQ275

Verified/Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture

For this item, refer to the KnightMotives Automotive case study. As part of developing fully autonomous driving vehicles, KnightMotives wants to analyze all vehicle-sensor data captured during test drives. This analysis will allow KnightMotives to improve its software using insights from the data.

  • Different event types, including parking, overtaking, and navigating, must be analyzed. Each test vehicle and event type has an ID.
  • Different sensor categories, including cameras, radars, and ultrasonic beams, must also be analyzed. During every autonomously initiated event, data from multiple sensors will be captured and sent to Google Cloud, where it will be stored in Bigtable.

During analysis, you need to retrieve all sensor data for occurrences of the same event type, for a particular vehicle, within a specified time interval. You need to design a Bigtable schema optimized for read performance. What should you do?

Explanation

Bigtable sorts row keys lexicographically. A row key ordered as vehicle ID, event ID, and timestamp places all records for a vehicle-event pair in one contiguous range and permits an efficient timestamp-bounded scan. Sensor categories are appropriate column families, and individual sensors within a category are appropriate column qualifiers. A timestamp should not be the leading key component for this access pattern.

This results in inconsistent and insecure deployments, including GKE clusters without appropriate logging and IAM roles that are overly permissive. You need to implement a system that enables these teams to deploy complete, pre-approved architectural patterns through self-service. The system must provide security and consistency by default while preserving high developer velocity and avoiding manual approval bottlenecks. What should you do?

Explanation

Google Cloud Service Catalog lets administrators curate and share approved solutions for internal users to discover and deploy. QuestionQ280

You are building a deep learning model that needs high-performance access to large volumes of media data currently held in Cloud Storage. Model training will run on multiple VM instances with attached GPUs, but the application must access the data as though it were on the local file system. You need to minimize cost and complexity. What should you do?

Explanation

Cloud Storage FUSE mounts a Cloud Storage bucket as a local file system, allowing applications to read and write bucket objects through standard file-system semantics. This avoids copying the dataset into Filestore, persistent disks, or each VM, reducing extra storage cost and operational complexity.

QuestionQ281

Verified/Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture

Your organization runs a 3-tier web application in the same Google Cloud Platform network. Each tier—web, API, and database—scales independently of the other tiers. Network traffic must pass from the web tier to the API tier and then to the database tier. Traffic must not pass directly between the web and database tiers.

How should you configure the network?

Explanation

Google Cloud VPC firewall rules control whether traffic is allowed or denied, and network tags let those rules apply to all instances in each scalable tier. Assign distinct tags to the web, API, and database tiers; allow web-to-API and API-to-database traffic with targeted firewall rules, and do not allow web-to-database traffic. Routes determine packet paths and do not provide this tier-to-tier access control.

QuestionQ282

Verified/Designing for security and compliance

Your company has a Google Cloud project that uses BigQuery for data warehousing. Some tables contain personally identifiable information (PII).

Only the compliance team can access the PII. All other information in the tables must be available to the data science team. You want to minimize cost and the time required to assign the appropriate table access. What should you do?

Explanation

An authorized logical view in a separate dataset can expose only the non-PII columns while allowing the data science team to query the view without direct access to the source dataset. Granting access to the view dataset and authorizing the view against the source dataset centralizes access management and avoids the additional storage and refresh cost of a materialized view.

QuestionQ283

Verified/Analyzing and optimizing technical and business processes

Your company wants to migrate its 10-TB on-premises database export to Cloud Storage. You want to minimize the time required to complete this activity, the total cost, and database load. Bandwidth between the on-premises environment and Google Cloud is 1 Gbps. You want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

Explanation

With a 1-Gbps connection, an online upload of a 10-TB export is practical; Google describes Transfer Appliance as especially suitable when network bandwidth is limited or unavailable, and notes that reasonable connectivity such as 1 Gbps can make online transfer appropriate. Compressing the existing export reduces the transfer volume without rereading the database, while gsutil -m performs operations in parallel to improve upload throughput. This avoids the shipping delay and added appliance cost, as well as the database load of extracting data through Dataflow or an ETL tool.

QuestionQ284

Verified/Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture

Your company runs AI/ML workloads on graphics processing units (GPUs) in Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). These workloads are deployed across production and development projects, and the production environment is business-critical and runs 24/7. You must ensure GPU capacity is always available during scaling events without being constrained by overall GPU availability. You also need to be able to shift unused GPU capacity from the production project to development projects as necessary. You want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

Explanation

Shared reservations guarantee capacity for matching GPU VM resources and can be consumed by multiple designated projects. Google recommends an owner project that creates and manages the shared reservations but does not consume them, with workload projects configured as consumer projects. This lets production and development draw from the same reserved capacity, maximizing use of capacity that production is not currently consuming.

Explanation

Google Cloud recommends mapping workload dependencies during discovery and assessment, then grouping interdependent workloads into migration waves and move groups. QuestionQ287

Verified/Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture

You are designing the storage architecture for a financial analytics platform. The platform ingests and retains terabytes of transactional data each day, which supports both real-time fraud detection and long-term historical analysis.

Transaction data from the most recent 30 days must be available with very low latency to the fraud-detection engine. Data more than 30 days old is accessed infrequently for quarterly reports, for which retrieval times of a few seconds are acceptable. All data must be retained for five years to satisfy compliance regulations.

You need to design the most cost-effective solution possible. What should you do?

Explanation

Coldline storage is designed for data read or modified at most once per quarter and provides low-latency online access at a lower storage cost than Standard storage. Keeping the most recent 30 days in Standard storage satisfies the fraud-detection latency requirement, while an Object Lifecycle Management policy can automatically transition older objects to Coldline for the five-year retention period. Archive storage is better suited to data accessed less than once per year and has higher access costs.

A branch-based Cloud Build trigger centrally runs the required tests and creates the container image whenever code is pushed to the remote develop branch. QuestionQ291

A primary business objective is to be able to trust the data stored in your application. You want to record every change to the application data.

How can you design the logging system to verify the authenticity of its logs?

Explanation

Digital signatures cryptographically bind each timestamp and log entry to the signer. A valid signature can be verified later, and any modification to the signed content invalidates it, providing evidence of log integrity and authenticity.

QuestionQ293

Verified/Ensuring solution and operations excellence

Your operations team has asked for help diagnosing a performance problem in a production application running on Compute Engine. The application drops requests that reach it under heavy load. The process list on affected instances shows one application process consuming all available CPU, and autoscaling has reached the instance upper limit. No other related systems, including the database, are experiencing abnormal load. You want production traffic to be served again as quickly as possible. Which action should you recommend?

Explanation

A CPU-saturated managed instance group that has reached its autoscaling maximum cannot add capacity despite continued demand. Raising the autoscaler's maximum number of instances permits scale-out and distributes requests across additional application instances. Compute Engine autoscaling adds VMs when CPU utilization exceeds the configured target, subject to the configured maximum.

QuestionQ300

Verified/Designing for security and compliance

A large multinational company is migrating to Google Cloud. It has distinct business units: Finance, Marketing, and Research and Development (R&D). The central security team has established the following governance requirements for each unit:

  • Finance: Must be limited to deploying resources only in the specific compliant regions us-central1 and europe-west2. Access to its projects must be strictly controlled by a dedicated finance-admins group.
  • Marketing: Requires separate production and development environments, with different teams responsible for managing each environment.
  • R&D: Needs maximum flexibility to test new services, but must be fully isolated so it cannot affect production systems.
  • Global Auditing: A central compliance team needs read-only access to view every resource across the entire company for auditing.

You must design a resource hierarchy that enforces these security policies at scale, follows the Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework, and provides each business unit with the appropriate level of autonomy. What should you do?

Explanation

Google Cloud folders are policy and IAM inheritance boundaries that support delegated administration, security isolation, and scalable governance. Applying the resource-location Organization Policy to the Finance folder constrains all descendant projects to the approved locations, while department folders allow separate administrative control and isolation. Separate Marketing production and development projects create distinct environment boundaries. Granting roles/viewer at the Organization level gives the compliance team inherited read-only access throughout the organization hierarchy.
